title: Finite Loop Safety Bounds
primary_claim: Every LoopBounds safety ceiling is a positive finite value, count ceilings retain integer semantics, and CLI-parsed NaN/Infinity are refused before LoopDriver construction.

baseline.finding: LoopBounds historically checked only float(value) <= 0, which admits NaN and positive Infinity.
impact: NaN can make wall-clock and spend comparisons permanently false
positive Infinity acts as an undocumented unlimited sentinel
non-finite bounds can leak into non-standard JSON receipts

acceptance: max_wall_clock_s and max_spend_usd reject NaN, positive Infinity and negative Infinity
max_iterations and max_attempts_per_candidate reject booleans and non-int programmatic values
positive finite bounds retain the existing public LoopBounds shape
LoopBounds.to_dict is serializable with json.dumps(..., allow_nan=false)
CLI nan/inf inputs return refusal before constructing LoopDriver
existing zero/negative/None refusal behavior remains intact

verification.hosted_ci: No exact-head result may be claimed unless a workflow executes real steps; issue #67 remains relevant to absent/zero-step jobs.

rollback: Drop this packet branch; no persisted schema, runtime registry, approval, promotion or Gate state is changed.
review_questions: Does validation fail closed before any LoopDriver/executor construction?
Are integer count bounds kept as integers rather than silently coerced?
Does the repair add no second budget or scheduling authority?
